newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes up, silver down on world trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes up, silver down on world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees higher at 4,750 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,730 rupees as shortage of ready stock and renewed seasonal support helped prices to bounce back after weak opening.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 250 rupees higher at 55,550 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,300 rupees. They were up by 100 rupees per piece on Wednesday.

** Silver (.999) closed 145 rupees lower at 7,130 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,275 rupees amid sharp losses in the world market as well as increased arrivals of imported silver. Silver was down by 55 rupees per kg on Wednesday.

Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees higher at 4,750 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,730 rupees as fresh seasonal buying and restricted arrivals dragged prices upward towards the close after lower start, dealers said.
Gold opened 10 rupees lower at 4,720 rupees but later on bounced back towards the close, they said.

Meanwhile prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed 250 rupees higher at 55,550 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,300 rupees after gaining 100 rupees on Wednesday. They opened today at 55,200 rupees but later on bounced back on seasonal support.

Silver (.999) on the other hand closed 145 rupees lower at 7,130 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,275 rupees on the back of sharp losses in the world market as well as increased arrivals of the imported silver, dealers said.
Silver was down by 55 rupees per kg on Wednesday.
"Industrial buyers kept sidelines in the falling market while arrivals in the imported silver rose today to 1,500/2,000 kg," one broker said. (Conversion $1=35.86 rupees)
